title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-02-14
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v10.2 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel (7 inch 1/2 Track at 15ips) -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording of a legendary Feb 1970 Fillmore East show – crisp Miller remaster and a peak performance highlighted by Dark Star, The Eleven, St. Stephen, Hard to Handle and Not Fade Away.
ai_review.review: The February 1970 double‑set captures the Dead at a transitional high point: the band is tight, the drummers explode, and songs like Dark Star, The Eleven, St. Stephen/Lovelight sandwich and Hard to Handle soar. Charlie Miller’s meticulous remaster makes the soundboard source clear and punchy, though the early set suffers a missing segment of The Eleven. Overall the musical payoff far outweighs any minor gaps.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 5‑star, praising both performance and sound; only a few 4‑star notes about minor cuts. Weighted show quality (≈4.5) plus excellent soundboard recording (≈4.8) yields an overall rating around 4.6.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Charlie Miller’s extra‑crispy remaster delivers clear, balanced audio; a few reviewers note a missing segment of The Eleven/St. Stephen in the early show, but overall sound is punchy with no noticeable tape hiss or dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑show format (early acoustic set then electric late set) flows smoothly; classic transitions like Dark Star > St. Stephen > The Eleven and the Lovelight sandwich are highlighted, with a high‑energy second set that keeps momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note Jerry’s fluid lead work and perfect tone throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers are described as "on point" and "explosive", with post‑drum sections especially praised.
